understand.concept: An address book stores contact records and supports sorting by name and searching by key. The comparison rule must be consistent and string storage must remain valid for every record.
understand.whyItMatters: This project integrates structures, string handling, sorting and searching, while exposing the relationship between sort order and search preconditions.

explain.narrative:
An address book stores contact records and supports sorting by name and searching by key. The comparison rule must be consistent and string storage must remain valid for every record.

For a complete implementation, define input constraints, ownership, error handling and test cases before coding. Compile with warnings and verify normal, boundary and failure behaviour.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: qsort uses the comparator to order records by name. After sorting, a compatible binary search can be used; a search using a different comparison rule would be incorrect.

practise.guidedTask: Predict which name appears first after sorting.
practise.independentTask: Add case-sensitivity policy, duplicate-name handling and binary search. Test empty and equal-name cases.
hints: Ensure strings are null-terminated before strcmp.
The comparator must define a consistent ordering.
Document whether names are compared case-sensitively and how locale affects ordering.
